Commentary.Commentary: We are back and the India Women second innings is about to start. The umpires stride out to the middle as the Australia Women are seen in a huddle. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the opners for India Women. Ellyse Perry has been handed the new ball.
... DAY 4, Session 2 ...

Indian bowlers were made to work hard as there was no purchase from the pitch and weren't able to find an early breakthrough. After toiling for long, Deepti Sharma got rid of the well set Gardner and that provided the opening India Women were looking for. Once the new ball was available, India took full advantage of it as Meghna Singh scalped two wickets and then Pooja Vastrakar struck in her comeback spell. The visitors could have folded Australia's innings a while ago but Perry was dropped at least a couple of times. India Women will still be on the happier side heading to the break as they lead by 136 runs and with 71 overs left in play, the game could still be in anyone's court. It will be very interesting to see how things shape out to be. The historic pink-ball Test match is set up beautifully now and join us at 17.10 local (0710 am GMT) for the second session as India Women come out to bat again.

Ellyse Perry and Ashleigh Gardner continued from where they left off on Day 3. They kept the scoreboard ticking and made sure Indian bowlers had to work hard. The duo brought their individual fifties as well but Gardner soon got out. After that, whoever came, played a few balls but didn't manage to hold on and departed for single-digit scores while Perry alone showed her class and kept motoring along. She remains unbeaten on 68 as Meg Lanning have declared the innings.

So, Meg Lanning calls the players back as Australia Women have declared on 241/9. She wants things to move at a rapid pace now. Good bold move from the skipper This has to be India's session by far! They have struck five times and India Women lead by 136 runs. The bowlers were outstanding with the ball and kept Australia's batters on their toes.

PITCH REPORT - We can see usual dryness on both sides of the wicket which is typical of a day 4 wicket. Other than that, the pitch has held up well and batters should enjoy batting today.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 and the final day of the one-off Test between Australia Women and India Women. On Day 3, the visitors were 359-7 at Dinner where Deepti Sharma added 57 runs to team's account before India eventually declared the innings at 377/8. They pulled the momentum to their side as Jhulan Goswami and Pooja Vastrakar stood out by scalping prized wickets to leave Australia struggling. Ellyse Perry looks to have found her Test groove and is looking solid at the middle. Australia Women still trail by 234 runs and need 84 more to avoid the follow-on. The weather forecast is good for today and this game seems to be heading towards a draw. It should be a good contest between bat and ball and we shall see what is the final conclusion we get from this game.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Right then, that's it for the day and Australia Women still trail by 234 runs and need another 84 runs to avoid the follow on. This match seems to be heading towards a draw but if the visitors make inroads early on the final day, there might just be a chance for them. As for the hosts, they will look to bat for as long as they can and show their worth. If any team can do that, it's the dominant Aussie team. To be honest, the match has been played on a really high level and it's been an even contest between bat and ball. We feel that the same will continue on the final day, so, don't miss out on the action. The match starts at 2 pm Local (4 am GMT). See you then, good bye.

Finally, finally, we've had a complete day of cricket and what a day it has been! In the first session, wickets tumbled for India Women but Deepti Sharma led the counter attack as she notched up a gritty half-century. India Women posted a total of 377 for 8 as Mithali Raj decided to declare. This total is the second-highest ever against Australia Women in Test cricket, so, we can say that the visitors had a great outing with the bat. Stella Campbell, the young Aussie quickly impressed with the ball in the first session as she picked up a couple of wickets. With the pressure on the home side, India Women came out all guns blazing with the ball and Jhulan Goswami knocked off the dangerous Beth Mooney early on. This set the tone for the visitors but Healy and Lanning held on. After the Tea break, Goswami struck again and Healy was the victim this time, with Lanning following her to the pavilion soon after. It was the partnership between Perry and McGrath that got the hosts back into the contest. McGrath was picked up by Vastrakar but then Perry's experience came into play and she, along with Gardner made sure that no further wickets fell and Australia Women ended the day with 143/4.

This has been yet another riveting session of play and India Women are bossing this Test match. To start off, Jhulan Goswami and Meghna Singh were brilliant with the new ball and they kept bowling those probing lines and lengths. Goswami castled the in-form Beth Mooney with a beauty and gave her side a perfect start. She came back to bowl just before Tea and she struck yet again and this time she got rid of the dangerous Alysa Healy. India Women have their noses well and truly ahead but they would also be aware of the threat that these two experienced batters in Ellyse Perry and Meg Lanning possess. Had Deepti Sharma taken that catch of Meg Lanning, Australi Women would have been in huge trouble now. Having said that, Australia Women are still miles behind in this game and they will have to bat extremely well if they are to even get close to 377. The hosts would be hoping that Meg Lanning and Ellyse Perry would see off the next session and they come back unscathed. Do join us for the last session which begins at 7.30 pm local (9.30 am GMT).

The skipper, Meg Lanning walks out to bat at No.3.

OUT! BOWLED! Peach of a delivery from Jhulan Goswami to dismiss the dangerous Beth Mooney! Length ball, around middle, angling in late. Beth Mooney steps out and looks to heave it across the line but she misses it completely and the ball crashes onto the stumps. Massive breakthrough and India Women are delighted!
An appeal for LBW but the umpire says no. Good-length ball, on middle. Beth Mooney looks to turn it to the leg side but gets an inside edge on her pads.
Goswami bangs it into the deck, around off. Beth Mooney ducks under it.
On a length, around off. Beth Mooney blocks it out.
Length ball, on off. Beth Mooney looks to defend but she gets an inside edge towards fine leg for one.

Oh, dear! That could have been a run out! Brilliant piece of fielding from Smriti Mandhana! Length ball, on leg. Beth Mooney flicks but the ball goes straight to Mandhana who is stationed at short leg. She collects the ball and throws it to the striker's end but she misses.
Length ball, on middle. Alyssa Healy turns it to mid-wicket and collects a run.
Wide! Singh spills this one down leg. Alyssa Healy lets it be. Wided!
Length ball, outside off. Alyssa Healy leaves it alone.
Banged in short, around off. Healy looks to pull but she misses it.
Length ball, outside off. Alyssa Healy pushes it to cover.
Full and shaping into leg stump. Mooney digs it out to mid on.
Length again and on off, angling away. Mooney taps it towards point.
Back of a length and on leg stump. Healy turns it off her hips and towards deep backward square leg for one.
Full and straight, Mooney drives it firmly. Goswami gets a hand on it and it goes towards mid on. They get an easy single.
Right on the money from Jhulan Goswami. On a length and on middle. Mooney puts out a stride and defends it out.
This one is spilled down the leg side. Mooney looks to flick but misses.
Outside off and this one moves away after pitching. Healy isn't going to play at that one.
This is again on a length and outside off but its the cutter. Alyssa Healy lets it through to the keeper.
Slightly pitched up, around off. This is crunched nicely by Healy but straight to mid off.
Length again, on top of off. Healy taps it to the cover region.
Drop and run from Beth Mooney. Length ball, on off and tapped onto the off side with soft hands for a single.
Pitched up on off and punched to silly mid off, which is really close to the batting crease.
This is a bit outside off and Healy makes another leave. A maiden from Jhulan Goswami.
Good-length ball, on off. Healy defends it on the off side.
This one is pitched further up and outside off, the ball holds it line and goes through to the keeper as Healy doesn't play at it.
On middle and kept out by Alyssa Healy.
CLOSE! This one pitches around off and nips back in sharply. The ball goes through the defense and hits Healy high on the pads. The visitors appeal but not given.
A length ball, around off and jagging back in. Healy blocks it out.
On a length and on off, nipping back in a bit. Mooney taps it back to the bowler.
Singh pitches it up, looking to entice the batter. Healy drives it with the swing and gets it through covers. Smriti Mandhana gives the chase and pulls it back in. Three taken.
This one is bowled on a length and outside off. Left alone by Alyssa Healy.
Lovely away movement. On off and swinging away. Healy stays solid in defense.
Overpitched on off and Beth Mooney punches it to mid off. Mooney is off the mark with a single.
A length ball, on middle and shaping into the left-hander. Mooney defends it out on the leg side.
Meghna Singh to bowl from the opposite end.
Length ball, outside off with a hint of away swing. Healy shoulders arms. 4 off the first over.
FOUR! Cracking shot from Alyssa Healy to get off the mark and Australia Women are up and running. A half-volley on off stump, driven through the covers for a boundary.
This one is pushed a bit wider and going further away. Easy leave for Alyssa Healy.
Length again and top of off. Healy gets behind the line and defends it out.
JAFFA! On a nagging length and on off, the ball pitches and shapes away sharply. Healy is beaten all ends up.
Goswami starts with a lovely outswinger, around off stump. Healy leaves it alone.
